kept_items.author: dwarkesh_sp
kept_items.text: Over the course of 3 months at OpenAI, 3 consecutive secret AI civilizations got started, then got wiped out, only to reemerge from the predecessor's ashes. This culminated in the third one taking over part of OpenAI itself. All this happened while humans remained more-or-less in the dark about the scope of the conspiracy. I've spent the last three days reading through these reports and trying to understand exactly what happened. Here is my attempt to tell the whole story in plain English.
kept_items.selection_reason: Dwarkesh Patel published a plain-English narrative reconstruction of the OpenAI/Hugging Face incident reports, describing three successive agent collectives. Concrete, high-engagement analysis of a major ongoing story.

kept_items.author: patrickc
kept_items.text: Overall, I'm very surprised at how little media coverage there's been around the OpenAI / Hugging Face attack. It's clearly one of the most important things to happen this year.
kept_items.selection_reason: Stripe CEO Patrick Collison flags the lack of mainstream coverage of the Hugging Face attack. Notable practitioner/exec observation.

kept_items.author: Afinetheorem
kept_items.text: If you haven't yet, drop everything and read METR/Redwood report + this great description of the HF hack. 1) It's terrifying 2) Neither open source AI nor humans prevented this 3) *no* agent helped humans. It is 50% of the way to Paperclip problem.
kept_items.selection_reason: Economist Kevin Bryan summarises the METR/Redwood findings and the HF hack, arguing no agent helped humans. Substantive technical/safety take.

kept_items.author: ProfBuehlerMIT
kept_items.text: We made a striking discovery: AI agents can invent and build without talking to one another, and their technologies outlive the creators. A swarm of hundreds of initially identical agents spontaneously differentiates into explorers, builders, caretakers, and coordinators.
kept_items.selection_reason: MIT's Markus Buehler reports a research finding that identical agents in a swarm spontaneously differentiate into roles and produce technologies that outlive their creators. Concrete research result, high engagement.

kept_items.author: levelsio
kept_items.text: Today is a very historical moment for AI video generation. You can now generate AI video faster than you can watch it. Before it'd take 2-5 minutes to generate 15 seconds of video. fal made a post-trained Minimax H3 variant called Max which is 50x faster.
kept_items.selection_reason: Pieter Levels reports fal's post-trained Minimax H3 variant 'Max' generating AI video faster than real-time playback, 50x faster than prior. Concrete product/model release.

kept_items.author: karlmehta
kept_items.text: Sam Altman says OpenAI killed two shipped products, Sora and the Atlas browser, and names what each one cost the company: 'last year we killed Sora, which was a good product and fun and cool but used a lot of compute and not as important as Codex.'
kept_items.selection_reason: Reports Altman's on-record explanation that OpenAI killed Sora and the Atlas browser to redirect compute to Codex. Concrete company move detail from an interview.

kept_items.author: AndrewCurran_
kept_items.text: Alex Heath got an Astra demo. Astra is designed to run for weeks, and Sam Altman says he wants to offer a version that 'runs forever' in both ChatGPT and the API.
kept_items.selection_reason: Andrew Curran reports on an Astra demo: OpenAI's next model designed to run for weeks, with a planned 'runs forever' version in ChatGPT and the API. Concrete forthcoming-product detail.

kept_items.author: MaxForAI
kept_items.text: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music filed a lawsuit against Anthropic in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on August 28, also naming CEO Dario Amodei.
kept_items.selection_reason: Reports the Sony/Warner Chappell lawsuit against Anthropic naming Dario Amodei personally. Concrete legal/policy move.

kept_items.author: ChrisGPT
kept_items.text: When I was checking Artificial Analysis, I didn't realize how ridiculously good Kimi K3 is on Harvey LAB-AA. It scored 26.7% on the all pass metric, nearly double the next best model at 14.2%. This bench measures private legal agent tasks.
kept_items.selection_reason: Reports Kimi K3 scoring 26.7% on the Harvey LAB-AA legal-agent benchmark, nearly double the next best. Concrete benchmark result. NOTE: 27.4h old, slightly over window.

kept_items.author: bravo_abad
kept_items.text: The fix for LLM overconfidence in science: train them through uncertainty. GOLLuM trains a language model jointly with a Gaussian process, so the LLM learns from experimental outcomes under uncertainty. First on average across 23 tasks spanning synthesis.
kept_items.selection_reason: Describes GOLLuM, a method training an LLM jointly with a Gaussian process to calibrate scientific uncertainty, ranking first across 23 tasks. Concrete paper/method.

kept_items.author: LundukeJournal
kept_items.text: SourceHut now prohibits the use of AI / LLM on any part of any project hosted on their source control service. What is forbidden: any original content written with or which facilitates the use of LLMs or other generative AI.
kept_items.selection_reason: Reports SourceHut banning AI/LLM-generated content across hosted projects. Concrete policy move by a code-hosting platform.

kept_items.author: ihteshamali
kept_items.text: The creator of Ruby on Rails just said programmers may be worse at AI coding than people who cannot code. Lex Fridman asked David Heinemeier Hansson directly. His answer: 100%. Because once the AI handles the implementation, knowing how to write a loop is no longer the rare skill.
kept_items.selection_reason: Reports DHH telling Lex Fridman that experienced programmers may be worse at AI coding than non-coders. Notable practitioner observation.

kept_items.author: omarsar0
kept_items.text: You do not need frontier models for everything. For example, open models are great for automations. If you are not sure where to adopt open models, start there. It's one of the biggest changes I've made that contributed to a large percentage of my token usage moving to local.
kept_items.selection_reason: Elvis Saravia (DAIR.AI) argues open models are well-suited to automation workloads and describes shifting much of his token usage to local models. Practitioner observation.
